correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts shore-size cases. A one-vertex shore selection cannot be both dominating and connected; with at least two vertices on each shore domination is automatic. Connectivity can fail only in the two-by-two case, and there exactly when the selected index sets coincide. Direct counting then gives the polynomial and all corollaries. The independent finite verifier reconstructs the definitions through n=8 without serving as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the canonical perfect-matching deletion of balanced bicliques, and connected domination polynomials are an active recent object. The theorem gives a natural complete infinite-family classification and full enumerator, quantifying exactly how a one-factor deletion alters the known complete-bipartite polynomial. It is materially stronger than the prior scalar connected domination number.
